headline: P0143 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of about 28% against about 2% expected, and it stays high on patients with no chronic conditions. This pattern is consistent with upcoding.
rationale: Of this provider's 343 claims, 96 are 99215 (28.0%). The expected share given patient complexity is 2.1% (z vs peers 3.45, risk-adjusted score 12.0). The excess does not come from a sicker panel. Most visits are on patients with 0 chronic conditions (152 visits) or 1 (111 visits). On those patients the provider bills 99215 25.0% and 23.4% of the time, while all providers bill it 2.1% and 3.4% of the time. On the few 5+ condition visits (2) the provider billed no 99215, against 29.8% for all providers. The sampled 99215 claims on low-complexity patients mostly carry routine acute diagnoses: upper respiratory infection J06.9 (C0066276, C0066590, C0066500), rash R21 (C0066483, C0066540), UTI N39.0 (C0066376, C0066558), low back pain M54.50 (C0066395, C0066431) and follow-up Z09 (C0066566). In the comparison sample the same patient P0143-N0060 was billed 99214 for R21 (C0066527), another patient's Z09 visit was billed 99213 (C0066563), and a 5-condition patient was billed 99214 (C0066400). Taken together, this is a pattern consistent with upcoding rather than a high-acuity panel. However, the claim lists are random samples, and no clinical documentation (notes, MDM, time) is in the packet. Without that documentation, no single claim can be judged.
next_steps: Request the medical records for the sampled 99215 claims on 0-1 condition patients (for example C0066276, C0066376, C0066483, C0066566). Audit each against 2021+ E/M MDM or total-time criteria.
Pull every 99215 claim on 0-1 condition patients, not just the sample, and tally the primary diagnoses. Measure how many are self-limited acute problems such as J06.9, R21, N39.0, M54.50 or Z09.
Check whether time-based billing is being claimed, and whether documented times support 40+ minutes.
Compare same-patient, same-diagnosis visits billed at different levels (for example patient P0143-N0060: C0066566 vs C0066527) to test whether level selection is consistent.
Look at whether the 0-1 chronic condition counts are under-captured, which would understate true complexity. Check prior diagnosis history before concluding.
